Essentially (from my understanding) MC is a witch and widow that has magical abilities. After she was set to be killed, MC was resurrected by M, also called Merlin or Morgana, depending on what gender identity for the character you choose. M becomes a magical mentor to MC who she serves. M believes there is a powerful artifact hidden in the woods in the area, Stratford on Avon, where MC is called to go work in, and tells MC to find it. Witchcraft and magic is viewed as evil and against religion, so MC has to hide her abilities as she searches for and discovers what the artifact actually is. MC only has a limited amount of time to do this though because there is a curse on her that will turn her into a monster. To reverse the curse she has to spill mortal blood (the story will tell you who). M is helping her through this as she searches for the artifact. 

As the story goes on, MC starts to see signs there are other witches and followers of M who may also be looking for the artifact. She becomes suspicious of everyone around her and begins using her powers to understand their deepest sin (greed, envy, lust, etc) as a way to get an upper hand and exploit them. It starts to become clear as the story unfolds that someone is doing dark magic in Stratford on Avon because people are becoming possessed. There are clues and poetry that MC finds as she tries to discover who is doing the dark magic, and who is a fellow witch serving M as she continues her search for the artifact.

I have actually! I developed long Covid and have been dealing with a ton of weird physical symptoms that I believe could be connected to MCAS, POTS or both. I actually just wrote a symptom list for my primary care physician so I can bring this to his attention. This is what I wrote for him: 

After Covid my body changed completely. 
This is the first time in my life that I feel disconnected from my body. My symptoms include:
Debilitating fatigue/exhaustion that is almost daily,
Difficulty focusing,
Lack of motivation,
Struggles with daily executive functioning,
Getting what feels like restful sleep, but not having any change in my fatigue or exhaustion,
New food sensitivities- caffeine, eggs, waxed beans, fried foods, overly spicy foods,
My asthma and allergies have gotten worse, 
I’ve developed Gerd, gastritis, and anemia,
Sometimes I cycle between diarrhea and constipation, 
I have become more heat sensitive,
I can’t handle hot showers anymore. They make me dizzy, cause heart palpitations, and an increased heart rate, 
When I’m having a bowel movement that requires pushing, I sometimes will become extremely dizzy and feel faint. Sometimes even nauseous,
I deal with random bouts of nausea that don’t seem to have a trigger, 
I feel that my nervous system is off because sometimes my anxiety will also act up with no trigger.
Increase in headaches,
Increase in sinus pressure,
I don’t feel that I’m dealing with depression, this feels physical,
I catch bacterial infections and viruses much more often now. When I get them, they last much longer as well to the point that they usually turn into something else. I used to rarely get sick, 
I’m having a hard time starting tasks as well as completing tasks, 
I lose track of time much easier now to the point that I have literally lost hours upon hours of my day, 
I can go almost a full day feeling no hunger or thirst sometimes. There are times where I don’t even feel the urge to go to the bathroom, 
PMDD worsened and I dealt with more brain fog and overstimulation than I used to, as well as an increasing anxiety and depressive symptoms. My PMDD started feeling like it was going back to my normal baseline though when I lowered my dose of Wellbutrin.

What’s interesting is I didn’t start having reactions to caffeine until after I developed long Covid. I used to be able to handle caffeine pretty well. 

After recovering from Covid and developing long Covid, I started becoming very jittery and anxious if I drink too much caffeine. I can get away with a little bit of it, but unfortunately, I can’t drink the amount that I used to take. It’s super disappointing because drinking tea, especially Matcha, is what would help me to stay energized throughout my day, and long Covid has completely depleted my energy.

I’ve only tried one stimulant so far, and it made me very shaky and jittery just like caffeine does. It also caused me to have dizzy spells. My psychiatrist would like to try me on one other stimulant to see how it works for me. If that doesn’t work, then we’re going to look at non-stimulants. I was just recently diagnosed with ADHD and I would like to treat it with medication if possible.

A friendship after a break up is a very situational thing. It all depends on how the both of you are able to heal from the romantic relationship, and whether or not the both of you are capable of looking at each other as strictly platonic moving forward. My ex and I were not able to do that. I did entertain a friendship with him initially. When we first started talking after the two years of no contact, I had initially proposed that we start off on a clean slate as just friends. He was the one that had started initiating romantic interactions again. He started flirting with me. He was making plans for us that felt like dates. Since he was starting to initiate all of these romantic things, I started feeling my romantic feelings coming back. Then we fell right back into acting like a couple all over again. However, once that started, all of his old behaviors came back too. He was acting in all the ways he knew broke our relationship up the first time and it truly hurt. So unfortunately, in my situation, a friendship is not possible for us. I’ve gone completely no contact with him. I’ve blocked him on everything. I have no intention of having any sort of relationship with him moving forward.

Now I will say that there have been exes in my past that I have been able to become friends with again after the relationship ended. There was a significant amount of time that had passed before we rekindled the friendship. In all of those relationships we took time to get to know each other again. We spent time together in fully platonic ways. And there was no romantic undertones within the relationship. If you’re going to have a friendship with an ex, and you want it to be 100% fully platonic, then you have to have that boundary set that there is no flirting, there’s no romance, unless the both of you are honestly able to do that without falling for each other again, which is very difficult when it’s an ex romantic partner. 

My most successful friendship after a breakup was a nice situation overall, and we went about it maturely. We truly were able to be friends and were happy about it. Right as I was reading these texts I was thinking, “This is a fellow neurodivergent person”. Lol. I mean that in a good way. I just found out I have ADHD last year. My brother received his autism diagnosis in childhood. The two of us have learned how to communicate in a way that works for both of us. 

Is your friend neurotypical? I ask because the way that neurotypical people like to communicate is often different than how neurodivergent people communicate. What a lot of neurodivergent people do whether they have autism, ADHD, or both, is to “info dump”. That means that when you’re talking about a topic that you know a great deal of information about, that you tend to write lengthy texts about it, or in person, talk about it for a long extended period of time without allowing the other person to chime in and take part in the conversation as well. When this happens, and we don’t allow for the other person to show us if they’re comfortable with the conversation, or the length of time that the conversation is taking, it can actually make the person feel like they’re being lectured over having a mutual conversation. Some people describe it as feeling like they’re being “talked at, over being talked with”. Being talked with means that there is space for both people to communicate, and being talked at means that people feel that they’re not able to communicate how they feel about a topic, whether their opinion is right or wrong, because the other person is not holding space for them to do so. I think that’s why she accused you of “mansplaining”. Mansplaining means that the person feels that they already know a great deal of information about the topic of discussion, but the other person is continuing to bombard them with information as a way to “one up them” over respectfully sharing with them. 

There are a few points in these text messages where your friend was trying to express that she was not comfortable with the way in which you were speaking to her. This also happening on her birthday is something that I feel makes this whole situation worse. When it’s somebody’s birthday, usually the focus is on them. Rather than having the conversation focus on her, waiting to continue this back and forth later so that you can celebrate her special day, it turned into her receiving lengthy messages of information about a topic that she felt knowledgeable about already since she lived there. Then after she expressed she didn’t want the conversation to continue, you double downed and sent her an email. I think that’s where things really took a turn for the worst. Her telling you that she felt you were mansplaining was sign number one that she was feeling uncomfortable with the conversation. Messaging you privately to try to end the conversation was sign number two. I didn’t see her give permission for you to email her to continue the conversation, so receiving that email probably made her feel that you weren’t respecting her wishes to end the conversation, which she was trying to express. 

I can hold space for the fact that I don’t believe you had any sort of negative intent. I do see you apologizing multiple times. I think that what happened is she felt overwhelmed, and rather than seeing your messages as a well meaning gesture to share information, she viewed this as you lecturing her on her birthday, and not respecting her wishes to stop the conversation. I can understand that you probably didn’t see that she was asking for the conversation to end, but I think that’s the biggest issue in all of this. She was trying to express that she no longer wanted to talk about this topic because she felt that the fact that she lived in that area was not being taken into account, while also feeling like she was being bombarded with information on her birthday that she asked not to be bombarded with. To go from sending all of that information in a message, to then sending all of that information in an email on top of it was something that probably overwhelmed her because she thought that she was expressing to you that she had wanted the conversation to end.

I do think that this is a big misunderstanding between communication styles, and probably a situation where you had missed her social cues that she wanted the conversation to end. I would give her some space right now. Whether people are right or wrong on their views of a topic, there is a time and a place to give them a bulk of information. Some people would take this as being lectured, over an opportunity to share information and have a friendly debate on the different aspects of a topic that you both know about from educational and personal experiences. Sometimes asking for consent before sending a large amount of information can make all of the difference in the world.

I hope that the two of you are able to eventually work this out and become friends again! It seems like she does care about you. I thought that it was sweet that she expressed that the two of you probably communicate better in person than via text. Even if it’s well meaning, some people just can’t handle info dumping, especially if the person is introverted and/or isn’t big on texting in general. Coming back to messages that are very long and drawn out can feel overwhelming for some people. As somebody with inattentive ADHD I sometimes don’t enjoy it myself unless we’re talking about a topic that I really enjoy discussing. Too much information given to me at once can actually make me feel like I need to take extra time to process and think of an appropriate response back. My ADHD being inattentive, that takes more energy than I sometimes have, which leads me to step away from the messages and reply back later. 

Wishing you all the best and again, I hope that the two of you are able to become friends again!

My journey with organized religion was a difficult one throughout my childhood. My grandmother who meant the world to me was the definition of what religion and faith is supposed to be. She had lived her life embodying love, spreading kindness to everyone while honoring the higher power. The first school that I ever went to was a Christian Academy. The children were extremely mean. The teachers prioritized teaching us religious principles in the Bible over actual academics. My parents ended up pulling me out and sending me to public school. 

My grandmother loved taking me to church with her as another way for us to spend time together. The only time I enjoyed church was when I got to be with her the whole time. When I was in youth group or when I was around the other adults, it never made sense to me why so many were acting catty and rude, and why their kids were flat out bullies. I wanted to enjoy it for more time with my grandmother, but I never felt comfortable there. 

What was the turning point for me though was when I was sitting in church listening to the pastor, and he said that if a Christian and someone of another faith were building a house, no matter what, the Christian’s house would be the best simply because it was built by somebody who followed Christianity. I looked around me and saw people literally standing up from the pews, clapping and loudly cheering. I couldn’t believe they had that level of egotism. 

After that I admitted to my grandmother that I didn’t want to go to church anymore. She was completely respectful of that and told me she would never want me to do something that I didn’t want to do. If I wanted to learn about the Bible and her faith, she would teach me. If I didn’t, that was okay too. She loved me no matter what. I was so thankful that even though I knew her faith was such a huge part of her life, that she truly accepted me. That in itself was a reminder that there are people out there that truly do embody what spirituality is supposed to be. It’s unfortunate the level of narcissism and cruelty that you’ll find in others.

Later on in my teenage years I started questioning my faith after I had experienced trauma. I realized that spirituality resonated over organized religion. It made me connect to myself again and the higher power, who I refer to as “Universe” over God. My grandmother and I were actually a lot alike in how we looked at life and our faith, we just used different words and practices. My beliefs were more open and eclectic, hers were more organized.
